reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's risk-off call (confidence 0.4). Credit, long bonds and the dollar did not confirm the tech-led bounce, and Nvidia reports on 11-17 under an interim CEO. Four trades go through as proposed and one is cut. VNQ is sold because its stored TLT clause has tripped: TLT is 3.65% below its 200-day and the stance is risk-off. The Skeptic's point that REITs are not yet trading the rate move is fair, but the clause was written for exactly this case. WMT is trimmed by a third ahead of its 11-19 print, which the company has now confirmed (L2). For the trim's test I use the Skeptic's fairer relative-to-SPY wording. IEF is sold under L8. The Market Analyst says duration is not hedging, and IEF is 0.8% from its stop. The Skeptic is right that BND fails the same L8 test, so I restate BND's role below as a low-volatility reserve, not an equity hedge, and name it the next sell candidate. EXEL is cut from $25 to $15 (L3). That keeps Health Care near 12.9% by bucket and the INCY+EXEL oncology pair under about 5%. EXEL's Q3 figures from 10-29 are not in the inputs either. KR is approved at $15 as a rotation within Staples. The sells should execute before the buys, as the Implicator advises, so Staples ends below today's 15.5%. I set KR's stop at $61.50, not $64, because $64 would have sat only about 4% under the blended cost. If everything fills, cash is about $86, roughly 13.8% of equity. I accept that for now because of the risk-off stance, the 11-17 Nvidia and 11-19 WMT prints, and no other proposals. Cash above the buffer should go into the favored sectors once those prints pass. L4 is not my reason for leaving it idle. Holdings check (L7), from the stop blocks: no price stop has tripped. IEF and BND are NEAR; IEF is being sold and BND's role is restated. VOO and VTI hold: SPY is 3.91% above its 200-day stop and RSP's 21-day return is +4.07%. WMT's XLP clause has not tripped (21-day +5.81%, above the +3% line). DPZ got a Baird upgrade with no filing. KR's cyber clause is unconfirmed. CARG, MSCI, VRSN, INCY, IDXX and FAST have no guidance cut or negative 8-K in the window. BND's risk-on clause cannot trip under a risk-off stance. CARG (Communication), VRSN (Technology) and FAST (Industrials) sit in sectors the Market Analyst avoids today. I keep them on low beta and quality, with no adds. Through thesis_updates I re-date the SPY 200-day for VOO and VTI and fix stale text (L6): VTI's weight figure, MSCI's 'adds a sector the book does not hold', and WMT's 'unconfirmed' date.

trades.thesis: VNQ's stored invalidation has tripped: TLT closes 3.65% below its 200-day average (past the 3% line) while the Market Analyst is risk-off, and he no longer favors the sleeve because of its rate sensitivity. At about 1.9% of equity it had no live premise left (L4). Short-term loss of about $0.06; do not rebuy within 30 days.
trades.invalidation: The sale is wrong if, within 20 sessions, VNQ beats SPY while TLT closes back above its 200-day average.

trades.thesis: Pre-print trim of the largest single stock (12.0% of equity) ahead of the company-confirmed 11-19 Q3 release, 4 trading days out, after nine or more sell-side PT raises in five sessions. A close-based stop does not protect against a gap on the print (L7). The rest stays because Staples is still a Market Analyst favored sector. Short-term gain of about $1.5 to $1.8; the lot is short-term whenever it is sold.
trades.invalidation: The trim is wrong if WMT beats SPY by more than 3 percentage points over the 5 sessions after the 11-19 print and does not cut guidance.

trades.thesis: Under L8, IEF's diversifier role is contradicted by the Market Analyst's 11-13 note: duration is not hedging, and IEF fell 1.91% over 5 days while SPY rose 3.29%. It is 2.09% below its 200-day, and the mark is 0.8% above the $89.50 stop. Its stored thesis already named it the first bond to cut. BND stays as the single bond reserve, with its role restated. Short-term loss of about $0.16; do not rebuy IEF within 30 days, including on a regime-off day.
trades.invalidation: The sale is wrong if IEF closes above $92.00 within 20 sessions.

The annual data predates the Q3 print, whose figures are not in the inputs.

This moves Staples exposure from WMT, trimmed before its 11-19 print, to KR, whose Q3 call is company-confirmed for 12-03. F-score 7 (fails roa_improved and current_ratio_improved), gp_sector_pct 0.890, CFO $7.31B against net income $1.02B. WMT and KR move together on down days (L3), so this is the same Staples factor bet with a later earnings date, and the bucket ends below today's 15.5% only with the WMT trim. KR's negative beta is a statistical artifact, not a hedge.
